Per the project's stored release convention, you cut a release by pushing a git tag named `vYYYY.MM.N`:

- `YYYY.MM` is the year and month.
- `N` is the release number within that month. The example in the memory is `v2026.09.2`.
- For this month, the first release would be `v2026.10.1`, unless one already exists. Check existing tags with `git tag -l 'v2026.10.*'` to pick the next `N`.

```
git tag v2026.10.1
git push origin v2026.10.1
```

CI then builds and publishes. Never publish by hand.

I found this only in the EngramDB memory. I searched the repo's markdown, YAML, TOML and JSON files and found no CI workflow, release script or docs describing it. I couldn't check what CI does after the tag push, such as required checks, changelog steps or approvals. Nothing in the repo confirms the convention, so ask whoever owns CI if you need those details.
